subject: Clarify: what happens to requests / outputs for EU accounts and deletion workflow
messages:
From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@brightbank.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: security@brightbank.com
Date: 2028-04-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick clarifications on default logs for EU accounts

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. A couple of follow-ups from the security team: we need a short, authoritative answer for two points so we can close our internal risk ticket. Could you confirm the defaults for EU-region accounts on Redwood hosted API? Specifically: 

1) What does Redwood store by default for a typical text/generation request? Do you keep the request (prompt) and the generated output? Any intermediate artifacts (e.g., KV cache dumps, streaming fragments) counted as "logs"?

2) If Brightbank requests deletion of a user session and associated artifacts under our contract, what is the exact workflow and timeline for data removal in the EU region? Is there any staged retention (e.g., tombstone/soft-delete) that persists beyond the requested deletion?

We need language we can paste into the ticket and share with audit. Thanks—Maria

Best,
Maria Gonzalez
Senior InfoSec Manager
Brightbank

On Tue, Apr 29, 2028 at 09:12 AM Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@brightbank.com> wrote:
> See security@brightbank.com for the ticket reference.

From: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@brightbank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-29T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick clarifications on default logs for EU accounts

Hi Maria — thanks for the precise questions. I wanted to give a clear customer-facing answer, and I've looped in Marissa and Karthik for the technical nuances. High-level answers first, followed by details.

High-level (copy/paste friendly):
- Default capture: For hosted Redwood API, we persist the incoming request (the request metadata and the text content unless the customer opts out) and the generated output by default.
- Ephemeral items: runtime-only artifacts such as in-memory KV cache and streaming fragments are transient and not persisted as durable logs by default. They are treated as ephemeral unless a customer uses features that explicitly persist them (e.g., long-term session logging enabled via account config).
- Deletion workflow (EU): When Brightbank requests deletion, we start an automated removal for the request/output artifacts in the EU region. Deletions are hard-deletes for customer-visible artifacts; there is a short tombstone period (up to 24 hours) used for replication coordination across zones but no customer-accessible content remains after the deletion completes.

More detail for your audit doc below. I will refine wording with Marissa/Karthik and attach our short factsheet.

--- Detailed notes ---
1) What we store by default
  - Request: By default hosted accounts capture request metadata (timestamps, model, route) and the request payload (prompt text) for diagnostic and quality monitoring purposes. Customers can opt out at the account level; we provide per-route opt-outs and SDK flags.
  - Generated output: We store the generated tokens/response as an artifact tied to the request record, used for billing reconciliation, debugging, and quality monitoring.
  - Derivatives: embeddings, reranking artifacts, or eval traces are stored only if those specific APIs are used.
  - Runtime artifacts: the KV cache and ephemeral streaming fragments are not written to the main telemetry store by default. They may be checkpointed transiently within the serving cluster for hot-warm failover but those checkpoints are TTL'd and not part of durable customer logs unless the account enables session recording.

2) Deletion path and timeline (EU hosted)
  - Initiation: deletion request via Console, API, or support ticket.
  - Propagation: automated workflow marks records for deletion and begins zone-coordinated hard-deletes.
  - Tombstone window: system-level tombstone exists to ensure replication and index integrity — practical impact is that objects are unreachable within minutes and fully purged within 24 hours in the EU region.
  - Backups & cold-store: regular backups are retained for disaster recovery on a separate schedule; backup retention does not carry customer-usable artifacts longer than our stated backup retention policy. We can accept contract addenda to limit backup windows for regulated customers.

CC: Marissa & Karthik — please confirm the backup handling sentence and whether 24 hours is the right maximum tombstone language for EU.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_data_retention_factsheet.pdf (summary), eu-deletion-workflow-diagram.png

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-29T13:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick clarifications on default logs for EU accounts

Tessa — thanks for the writeup. A couple of nitpicks for audit accuracy (copying suggested edits inline):

- Tombstone window: we shouldn't promise an exact global SLA of 24 hours for every edge case. Suggested phrasing: "Objects become unreachable within minutes; replication tombstones are retained only for replication coordination and are normally cleared within 24 hours. For enterprise customers requiring stricter guarantees, we offer contractual terms with shorter retention on backups and additional deletion verification steps."

- Backups: we need to distinguish warm snapshots (used for fast restore) versus long-term immutable backups. Warm snapshots in the EU region are pruned on a retention schedule; immutable backups may exist per DR policy. Suggested add: "Brightbank can request a backup-scope scrub as part of a deletion order; this is processed separately and may take additional time depending on archive medium."

- Prompt vs derivative language: add the phrase "prompts and generated outputs are treated as primary artifacts and retained unless the account disables capture" so auditors understand derivatives are conditional.

Karthik — can you confirm the KV checkpointing behavior: they are ephemeral, TTL'd (minutes) and not available in our telemetry store? Also confirm whether session recording must be explicitly enabled by account admin.

Marissa Cole
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference

From: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@brightbank.com>
Cc: security@brightbank.com, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-30T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick clarifications on default logs for EU accounts

Hi Maria — following internal confirmation, here is a concise, audit-ready summary you can paste into Brightbank's ticket: 

1) Default capture for hosted EU accounts- Prompts and generated outputs: retained by default as primary artifacts for billing, debugging, and quality monitoring. Customers may opt out of capturing prompt content at the account or route level.
- Runtime-only artifacts (e.g., in-memory KV cache, streaming fragments): not persisted to durable telemetry by default. These are ephemeral and TTL'd within the serving cluster; session recording (which persists these artifacts) is an opt-in feature.

2) Deletion workflow and timeline (EU hosted)- Initiation: deletion request via Console/API/support ticket.- Propagation: records are marked and deleted in-region; objects are typically made unreachable within minutes and replication tombstones are cleared within 24 hours under normal operations.- Backups: warm snapshots are on a separate retention schedule. We can process a backup-scope scrub as part of a deletion order; timing depends on archive medium and will be scoped in the deletion confirmation.

If you need a short sentence for audit: 
"Redwood retains prompts and generated outputs by default for hosted accounts in the EU. Runtime-only serving artifacts are ephemeral unless session recording is explicitly enabled. Upon an authorized deletion request, customer artifacts are made unreachable within minutes and cleared from replication tombstones within 24 hours; backup-scope scrubs can be requested as a separate action and may take additional time."

I've attached our one-page factsheet as well as a simple diagram of the deletion propagation flow (see attachments). Happy to hop on a quick call with your security team if they'd like walk-throughs or a contractual deletion addendum.

Best regards,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_data_retention_factsheet.pdf, eu-deletion-workflow-diagram.png
